result.topic_en: Euler notes that an elastic lamina whose lower end is at a point of inflection (zero curvature) can merely rest on the floor in labile equilibrium under its own weight, and then argues that for the column problem a horizontal force must be applied at the upper end A to keep both ends on the same vertical line.

§. 5. Praeterea vero in hac curua infinita dabuntur puncta, quae littera O deſignauimus, vbi datur punctum flexus contrarii, atque adeo curuatura prorſus euaneſcit; vnde ſi infimus laminae elaſticae terminus in tali puncto accipiatur, non opus eſt, vt pauimento infigatur ſecundum ſuam directionem, ſed ſufficiet vt ſimpliciter inſiſtat, et talis lamina ob proprium pondus figuram exhibitam recipere et in aequilibrio conſiſtere poterit. Veluti ſi inferior laminae terminus in puncto O' capiatur, isque ſimpliciter pauimento E F inſiſtat, tum ob ſolum proprium pondus lamina inflecti poterit ſecundum curuam O' N G M A, hocque ſtatu in aequilibrio perſiſtere, propterea quod totius huius laminae centrum grauitatis G perpendiculariter puncto O' imminebit; euidens autem eſt, hunc ſtatum aequilibrii eſſe labilem, et laminam minima vi eſſe prolapſuram.

§. 6. Hinc iam clariſſime intelligimus, nullum horum caſuum ad quaeſtionem propoſitam accommodari poſſe, quippe qua eiusmodi columna conſideratur, cuius vterque terminus perpetuo in eadem recta verticali firmiter retineatur, dum in omnibus his caſibus ſupremo termino A plena libertas conceditur; quamobrem, vt noſtram quaeſtionem rite euoluamus, ſtatum columnae, ſiue laminae elaſticae, initialem aliter conſtituere debemus atque ante fecimus, ſcilicet praeter ſollicitationes a grauitate oriundas ſupremo termino A certam quandam vim horizontalem applicatam concipere debemus, qua iſtud punctum A perpetuo in eadem recta verticali contineatur. items.quote: ſi infimus laminae elaſticae terminus in tali puncto accipiatur, non opus eſt, vt pauimento infigatur ſecundum ſuam directionem, ſed ſufficiet vt ſimpliciter inſiſtat, et talis lamina ob proprium pondus figuram exhibitam recipere et in aequilibrio conſiſtere poterit.
items.english: If the lowest end of the elastic lamina is taken at such a point, it need not be fixed into the floor along its direction, but it suffices that it simply rest on it, and such a lamina can take the shown figure under its own weight and remain in equilibrium.

items.quote: euidens autem eſt, hunc ſtatum aequilibrii eſſe labilem, et laminam minima vi eſſe prolapſuram.
items.english: It is evident, however, that this state of equilibrium is labile and that the lamina will fall over under the smallest force.

items.quote: vt noſtram quaeſtionem rite euoluamus, ſtatum columnae, ſiue laminae elaſticae, initialem aliter conſtituere debemus atque ante fecimus, ſcilicet praeter ſollicitationes a grauitate oriundas ſupremo termino A certam quandam vim horizontalem applicatam concipere debemus, qua iſtud punctum A perpetuo in eadem recta verticali contineatur.
items.english: To work out our question properly, we must set up the initial state of the column, or elastic lamina, differently than before: besides the forces arising from gravity, we must conceive a certain horizontal force applied at the top end A by which that point A is kept always on the same vertical line.
